literal: He lectured between Yan and Zhao; the disciples who followed him were many.
idiomatic: He taught between Yan and Zhao, and the disciples who trailed after him were a great crowd.

literal: Whenever he gave instruction the Prince of Hejian Commandery would pursue him; [the prince] meant to recommend him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he firmly declined and would not accept.
idiomatic: Whenever he taught, the Prince of Hejian Commandery would press close upon him and meant to put him forward as Filial and Incorrupt; Jingde refused outright and would not take the post.

literal: So he went to the province to seek nomination as Emeritus Scholar.
idiomatic: So he went to the province and asked to be nominated as Emeritus Scholar.

literal: By rule Emeritus Scholar nominations took literary men; the provincial commander, seeing he was a pure Confucian, had no wish to recommend him.
idiomatic: Emeritus Scholar nominations were supposed to go to men of letters; the provincial commander, seeing a pure Confucian before him, had no mind to recommend him.

literal: Jingde requested a trial on strategy and tactics, so [the commander] questioned him in that vein; of the five answers he gave, each had literary sense.
idiomatic: Jingde asked to be tested on strategy and tactics instead. The commander put policy questions to him; all five of his answers were literate and sound.

literal: [The commander] then gladly sent him on to the capital with recommendation.
idiomatic: The commander was pleased and sent him on to the capital with his recommendation.

literal: Per the Emeritus Scholar policy questions, he only achieved middling rank; then he requested examination in classical studies—of ten questions he answered all correctly.
idiomatic: On the Emeritus Scholar policy examination he only reached middling rank; then he asked to be tested in the classics and answered all ten questions correctly.

literal: He was promoted and appointed Adjunct of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, then transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: He was promoted to adjunct of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, then transferred to erudite of the Imperial Academy.

literal: At the start of Tiantong he was made Erudite of the Directorate of the Sons of the State.
idiomatic: At the start of Tiantong he was made erudite of the Directorate of the Sons of the State.

literal: When Shizu chose tutors for the Later Lord, Zhao Yanshen recommended him; he entered [court] as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
idiomatic: When Shizu was choosing tutors for the Later Lord, Zhao Yanshen put him forward and he entered court as lecturer-in-attendance.

literal: His wife dreamed a fierce beast was coming toward her; Jingde ran and leaped through a bramble thicket, while his wife lay flat on the ground and dared not move.
idiomatic: His wife dreamed a fierce beast was bearing down on her. Jingde ran and vaulted through a bramble thicket; his wife lay flat on the ground and did not dare stir.

literal: Jingde divined and said: "I am about to receive high office.
idiomatic: Jingde read the dream and said, "I am about to receive high office.

literal: Leaping the thicket surpasses the Nine Ministers.
idiomatic: Vaulting the thicket means passing the Nine Ministers.

literal: You lying flat—that is the wife of a grandee."
idiomatic: You lying flat—that is the wife of a grandee."

literal: The Later Lord by then cared little for study; Jingde's lecturing was very sparse, but from time to time he would enter and teach the Spring and Autumn.
idiomatic: By then the Later Lord cared little for learning; Jingde's lectures grew thin, though now and then he would come in and teach the Spring and Autumn.

literal: At the start of Wuping, still in gratitude for tutor's favor, he was advanced to Director of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, given additional rank as Full Powers Equal to the Three Dukes and Grand Master with Golden Cap and Purple Tassel, made Grand Rectifier of Ying Province, and died in office.
idiomatic: At the start of Wuping, still out of gratitude for his service as tutor, he was advanced to director of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, given full powers equal to the three dukes and the golden-cap grand master rank, made grand rectifier of Ying Province, and died in office.

literal: Posthumously he was given Commander Who Opens a Government Office and Governor of Ying, Cang, and An provinces in military affairs over Ying.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the rank of commander who opens a government office and governor of Ying, Cang, and An provinces in military affairs over Ying.

literal: Afterward the attendant calligrapher Zhang Jingren was enfeoffed as prince.
idiomatic: Afterward the attendant calligrapher Zhang Jingren was enfeoffed as a prince.

literal: Zhao Yanshen said: "How can an attendant calligrapher be made prince while the lecturer-in-attendance has no enfeoffment or rank?"
idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen said, "How can an attendant calligrapher be made a prince while the lecturer-in-attendance has no title at all?"

literal: So Jingde too was enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghan Commandery.
idiomatic: So Jingde too was enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghan Commandery.

literal: His son Yuanxi inherited.
idiomatic: His son Yuanxi inherited the title.

literal: Yuanxi, styled Changming, in youth transmitted his father's learning and also cultivated literary polish.
idiomatic: Yuanxi, styled Changming, in youth took up his father's learning and also cultivated literary polish.

literal: Because of his father he was advanced from collection-office staff officer in Qing Province to attendant gentleman through direct access, awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall, and was made a regular appointee.
idiomatic: Because of his father he was vaulted from collection-office staff officer in Qing Province to attendant gentleman through direct access, awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall, and was made a regular appointee.

literal: In Wuping the heir apparent was about to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; the authorities asked to choose tutors and companions. The emperor said: "Ma Yuanxi is my tutor's son; his letters are not bad—let him teach the boy."
idiomatic: In Wuping the heir apparent was to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and the authorities asked who should teach him. The emperor said, "Ma Yuanxi is my tutor's son; his letters are not bad—let him teach the boy."

literal: So he entered to teach the Classic of Filial Piety to the heir apparent, and Confucians gloried that the office ran in the family.
idiomatic: So he came in to teach the Classic of Filial Piety to the heir apparent, and the Confucians took pride that the post had stayed in one line.

literal: His nature was mild and generous; within the palace he won great repute, and the heir apparent too treated him with personal respect.
idiomatic: His nature was mild and generous; within the palace he won great repute, and the heir apparent treated him with personal respect.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died as literary aide to the Prince of Qin.
idiomatic: In Sui's Kaihuang era he died as literary aide to the Prince of Qin.

literal: Zhang Jingren was a man of Jibei.
idiomatic: Zhang Jingren was a man of Jibei.

literal: Orphaned young and poor, he took up the study of writing as his craft, and came to excel at cursive and clerical script; he was selected and made up as an inner calligraphy student.
idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he took up writing as his trade and came to excel at cursive and clerical script; he was selected and made up as an inner calligraphy student.

literal: With Yao Yuanbiao of Wei Commandery, Han Yi of Yingchuan, Yuan Mainu of the same commandery, and Li Chao of Xingyang he was famed alike; Shizong brought them all in as guests.
idiomatic: With Yao Yuanbiao of Wei Commandery, Han Yi of Yingchuan, Yuan Mainu of the same commandery, and Li Chao of Xingyang he stood among the famous; Shizong brought them all in as guests.

literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao an edict appointed him to write for Prince of Taiyuan Shaode and made him staff officer who opens a government office.
idiomatic: In Tianbao's eighth year an edict appointed him to write for Prince of Taiyuan Shaode and made him staff officer who opens a government office.

literal: When the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace, Shizu chose men skilled at writing whose conduct was pure and cautious to serve as attendant calligraphers; Jingren was then brought forward and promoted.
idiomatic: When the Later Lord was still in the Eastern Palace, Shizu chose men skilled at writing whose conduct was pure and cautious to serve as attendant calligraphers, and Jingren was brought forward and promoted.

literal: Careful and reverent, he was loved by the Later Lord, who called him "Doctor."
idiomatic: Careful and reverent, he won the Later Lord's favor; the lord called him "Doctor."

literal: He passed through gate master of the heir apparent, supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office, and grand advisor for remonstrance.
idiomatic: He passed through gate master of the heir apparent, supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office, and grand advisor for remonstrance.

literal: When the Later Lord took the throne he was made attendant at the scribal office through direct access.
idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne he was made attendant at the scribal office through direct access.

literal: When the memorial was submitted, the imperial brush struck through the character "through" and he became regular attendant at the scribal office.
idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the imperial brush struck through the word "through," and he became regular attendant at the scribal office.

literal: Those close to him in speech still called him Doctor.
idiomatic: Those close to him still called him Doctor in conversation.

literal: The barbarian Hong Zhen had the Later Lord's favor and wished to marry his clan to court gentlemen; because Jingren's inner-court post was somewhat high, [Hong Zhen] took Jingren's second son Ziyu's daughter for his elder brother's son.
idiomatic: The barbarian Hong Zhen had the Later Lord's favor and wished to marry his kin into the court; because Jingren's inner-court post was somewhat high, he took Jingren's second son Ziyu's daughter for his elder brother's son.

literal: Through this inside-out tie, favor and grace grew daily.
idiomatic: Through that inside-out tie, favor and grace grew day by day.

literal: Jingren was often ill; each time [the court] sent Xu Zhifan and others to treat him, giving medicines and delicacies; palace envoys inquired after his illness one after another along the road.
idiomatic: Jingren was often ill; each time the court sent Xu Zhifan and others to treat him with medicines and delicacies, while palace envoys asking after his health filed along the road.

literal: After that, an edict ordered the authorities always to send imperial food to his residence.
idiomatic: After that an edict ordered the authorities always to send imperial food to his house.

literal: He was moved to acting full powers equal to the three dukes and grand master with silver cap and bluegreen tassel, drawing dry rations from Hengshan county.
idiomatic: He was moved to acting full powers equal to the three dukes and grand master with silver cap and bluegreen tassel, drawing dry rations from Hengshan county.

literal: When the imperial carriage went out on progress, at each night's lodging along the way they would send portable screens to keep off wind and cold.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went out on progress, at each night's lodging along the way they sent portable screens to keep off wind and cold.

literal: He advanced to full powers equal to the three dukes; soon he was further given commander who opens a government office, while attendant calligrapher and his other posts remained as before.
idiomatic: He advanced to full powers equal to the three dukes; soon he was further given commander who opens a government office, while his post as attendant calligrapher and his other offices stayed as they were.

literal: Each morning he had to attend court and would lodge in the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: Each morning he had to attend court and lodged in the Eastern Palace.

literal: When the Wenlin Hall was established, the inner attendant Deng Changyu, to please [the ruler], memorialized that [Jingren] should oversee the hall's affairs; he was made palace attendant.
idiomatic: When the Wenlin Hall was established, the inner attendant Deng Changyu, to please the ruler, memorialized that Jingren should oversee the hall; he was made palace attendant.

literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.

literal: After Hong Zhen died, Changyu still kept the old bond and they continued to smooth things over for each other, so he did not fall back.
idiomatic: After Hong Zhen died, Changyu still kept the old bond; they continued to smooth things over for each other, and Jingren did not fall back.

literal: He was made director of the masters of writing and died of illness.
idiomatic: He was made director of the masters of writing and died of illness.

literal: Posthumously he was given palace attendant, governor of the five provinces Qi, Ji, and others, and minister of works.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was given palace attendant, governor of the five provinces Qi, Ji, and others, and minister of works.

literal: Jingren came from humble beginnings and originally had no discernment; in a single stroke he became commander who opens a government office, palace attendant, and prince.
idiomatic: Jingren came from humble beginnings and originally had no discernment; in a single stroke he became commander who opens a government office, palace attendant, and prince.

literal: His wife's surname was Qi; no one knew what clan she came from. Her bearing, voice, and speech were vulgar in every respect.
idiomatic: His wife's surname was Qi; no one knew what clan she came from. Her bearing, voice, and speech were vulgar in every respect.

literal: Once she was enfeoffed by edict as princess consort and stood in the same court-audience order as the princesses and commandery ladies, those who saw her felt shame and alarm for her.
idiomatic: Once she was enfeoffed by edict as princess consort and stood in court-audience with the princesses and commandery ladies; those who saw her felt shame and alarm on her behalf.

literal: His son Ziyu thinly transmitted his father's craft and had no other skill; because of Hong Zhen he was advanced to drafting officer of the masters of writing, then moved to attendant gentleman at the yellow gate who serves matters.
idiomatic: His son Ziyu thinly transmitted his father's craft and had no other skill; because of Hong Zhen he was advanced to drafting officer of the masters of writing, then moved to attendant gentleman at the yellow gate who serves matters.

literal: His eldest son Ziyu began his career as supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office.
idiomatic: His eldest son Ziyu began his career as supernumerary attendant gentleman at the scribal office.

literal: Jingren's nature was originally humble, but once he used the power of the barbarian eunuch chamberlain he rose to conspicuous eminence; his resolve changed somewhat and he gradually grew proud.
idiomatic: Jingren's nature was originally humble, but once he rode the barbarian eunuch chamberlain's power to conspicuous eminence his resolve shifted and he gradually grew proud.

literal: Fine horses and light furs, attendants in a throng, high gates and broad halls facing the crossroads.
idiomatic: Fine horses and light furs, attendants in a throng, high gates and broad halls facing the crossroads.

literal: His sons did not reflect on their origins and styled themselves noble wanderers.
idiomatic: His sons did not reflect on their origins and styled themselves noble wanderers.

literal: Since Cang Jie, of those who advanced through the eight script styles, he alone.
idiomatic: Since Cang Jie, of those who advanced through the eight script styles, he alone.

literal: Quan Hui, styled Zhengli, was a man of Mo in Hejian.
idiomatic: Quan Hui, styled Zhengli, was a man of Mo in Hejian.

literal: His aims were deep and refined; in movement he followed ritual rule.
idiomatic: His aims were deep and refined; in movement he followed ritual rule.

literal: In youth he received Zheng's Changes, probing the hidden and seeking the obscure until he had exhausted the subtle; in the Odes, Documents, and Three Rites his literary meaning was comprehensive; he was also clear in wind and horn divination and had fine insight into dark signs.
idiomatic: In youth he studied Zheng's Changes, probing the hidden until he had exhausted the subtle; in the Odes, Documents, and Three Rites his literary meaning was comprehensive; he was also clear in wind and horn divination and had fine insight into dark signs.

literal: At the start of Wei Wuding his native commandery presented him as Filial and Incorrupt; in policy examination he ranked at the top and doffed the headcloth as erudite of the Four Gates.
idiomatic: At the start of Wei Wuding his native commandery presented him as Filial and Incorrupt; in policy examination he ranked at the top and doffed the headcloth as erudite of the Four Gates.

literal: Supervisor Cui Xian brought him in as hall guest and greatly respected him, ordering the heir Da to perform all a tutor's rites toward him; Hui thereby became known.
idiomatic: Supervisor Cui Xian brought him in as hall guest and greatly respected him, ordering the heir Da to perform all a tutor's rites toward him; Hui thereby became known.

literal: Xian wished to recommend Hui together with Ma Jingde and others as tutors to the princes; Hui's nature was tranquil and he did not covet glory or power, ashamed of left-hand office—he firmly declined.
idiomatic: Xian wished to recommend Hui together with Ma Jingde and others as tutors to the princes; Hui's nature was tranquil and he did not covet glory or power, ashamed of left-hand office, and firmly declined.

literal: Xian also understood his intent and so stopped the recommendation.
idiomatic: Xian also understood his intent and stopped the recommendation.

literal: Soon he was pursued by an order from the masters of writing to serve as author, revise the national history, and oversee affairs of the Directorate of Astronomy.
idiomatic: Soon he was pursued by an order from the masters of writing to serve as author, revise the national history, and oversee affairs of the Directorate of Astronomy.

literal: In Huangjian he was further made grand master of the scattered cohort; the rest remained as before.
idiomatic: In Huangjian he was further made grand master of the scattered cohort; the rest remained as before.

literal: Though his concurrent duties were many, he did not neglect teaching.
idiomatic: Though his concurrent duties were many, he did not neglect teaching.

literal: His nature was very Confucian and timid, as if he could not speak; yet when facing a challenge on the spot his replies came like an echo.
idiomatic: His nature was very Confucian and timid, as if he could not speak; yet when facing a challenge on the spot his replies came like an echo.

literal: In movement he always checked against antiquity; his words were never empty—therefore the Confucian leaders pushed him forward.
idiomatic: In movement he always checked against antiquity; his words were never empty, and the Confucian leaders pushed him forward.

literal: Yet noble wanderers' sons who admired his virtue and righteousness would come to his house or lodge with neighbors nearby, day and night seizing intervals to receive his learning.
idiomatic: Yet sons of noble wanderers who admired his virtue and righteousness would come to his house or lodge with neighbors nearby, day and night seizing intervals to receive his learning.

literal: Hui would lecture gladly and never slacken.
idiomatic: Hui would lecture gladly and never slacken.

literal: Though he was clear in wind and horn and understood dark signs, in private quarters he never spoke of them; when students asked, in the end he said nothing.
idiomatic: Though he was clear in wind and horn and understood dark signs, in private quarters he never spoke of them; when students asked, in the end he said nothing.

literal: He would always say: "This learning can be known but cannot be spoken.
idiomatic: He would always say, "This learning can be known but cannot be spoken.

literal: You are all sons of noble wanderers; you do not advance by this path—why trouble to ask?"
idiomatic: You are all sons of noble wanderers; you do not advance by this path—why trouble to ask?"

literal: Hui had only one son and did not teach him this art either; such was his caution and secrecy.
idiomatic: Hui had only one son and did not teach him this art either; such was his caution and secrecy.

literal: Once he sent a household member on a distant journey who was long in returning.
idiomatic: Once he sent a household member on a distant journey who was long in returning.

literal: When the traveler came back, just about to reach the house, he met with cold snow and lodged at another inn.
idiomatic: When the traveler came back, just about to reach the house, he met with cold snow and lodged at another inn.

literal: Hui was in the lecture hall giving instruction when suddenly a whirlwind flashed by and blew snow into the room.
idiomatic: Hui was in the lecture hall giving instruction when suddenly a whirlwind flashed by and blew snow into the room.

literal: Hui then laughed and said: "The traveler has arrived—why stop midway?"
idiomatic: Hui then laughed and said, "The traveler has arrived—why stop midway?"

literal: He then ordered a man sent to seek him at a certain place; it turned out exactly as he had said.
idiomatic: He then ordered a man sent to seek him at a certain place; it turned out exactly as he had said.

literal: Whenever he divined for others, great or small, he always hit the mark.
idiomatic: Whenever he divined for others, great or small, he always hit the mark.

literal: But he used only the line texts and the judgment images to distinguish fortune and misfortune; divination of the Changes sort he never spoke from his mouth.
idiomatic: But he used only the line texts and the judgment images to distinguish fortune and misfortune; divination of the Changes sort he never spoke from his mouth.

literal: Hui was originally a poor student with no servants; in his first days as adjunct he always rode a donkey up and down.
idiomatic: Hui was originally a poor student with no servants; in his first days as adjunct he always rode a donkey up and down.

literal: Moreover his duties lay in many places and he had to pass through them constantly; when he left office for the day he did not return until late.
idiomatic: Moreover his duties lay in many places and he had to pass through them constantly; when he left office for the day he did not return until late.

literal: Once at night he went out the eastern gate; the clepsydra had already run out and Hui rode his donkey alone.
idiomatic: Once at night he went out the eastern gate; the clepsydra had already run out and Hui rode his donkey alone.

literal: Suddenly there were two men—one leading the head, one following behind—as if helping; their turning and movement were light and drifting, unlike living men.
idiomatic: Suddenly there were two men—one leading the head, one following behind—as if helping; their turning and movement were light and drifting, unlike living men.

literal: Gradually they lost the road and did not follow the original path.
idiomatic: Gradually they lost the road and did not follow the original path.

literal: Hui thought it very strange and so recited the upper part of the Book of Changes.
idiomatic: Hui thought it very strange and so recited the upper part of the Book of Changes.

literal: Before one scroll was finished the two men before and behind suddenly scattered.
idiomatic: Before one scroll was finished the two men before and behind suddenly scattered.

literal: Hui also did not notice he had fallen from the donkey and so grew dizzy; only at dawn did he come to.
idiomatic: Hui also did not notice he had fallen from the donkey and grew dizzy; only at dawn did he come to.

literal: Then he knew the place where he had fallen from the donkey was outside the city wall, only a few li from home.
idiomatic: Then he knew the place where he had fallen from the donkey was outside the city wall, only a few li from home.

literal: He had one son, styled Zixi, clever, keen, and diligent in youth, with the measure of a grown man.
idiomatic: He had one son, styled Zixi, clever, keen, and diligent in youth, with the measure of a grown man.

literal: Unfortunately he died first; those who escorted him wept in grief for him, but Hui wept only once and stopped—men of the time admired his acceptance of fate.
idiomatic: Unfortunately he died first; those who escorted him wept in grief, but Hui wept only once and stopped—men of the time admired his acceptance of fate.

literal: In the Wuping years, returning from his office to his residence, on the road for no reason his horse fell; he could not speak and so died suddenly, aged seventy-six.
idiomatic: In the Wuping years, returning from his office to his residence, on the road for no reason his horse fell; he could not speak and died suddenly, aged seventy-six.

literal: He annotated one work on the Changes, which circulated in the world.
idiomatic: He annotated one work on the Changes, which circulated in the world.

literal: All his life Hui feared horses; the rank and eminence he reached forced him to ride, and in the end it was by this that he perished.
idiomatic: All his life Hui feared horses; the rank and eminence he reached forced him to ride, and in the end it was by this that he perished.

literal: Zhang Sibai was a man of Yuecheng in Hejian.
idiomatic: Zhang Sibai was a man of Yuecheng in Hejian.

literal: Skilled at expounding Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, he stood second to Ma Jingde.
idiomatic: Skilled at expounding Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, he stood second to Ma Jingde.
